Scope addendum (filer) · #31732 · 2026-11-09T00:48Z

This card also carries the MariaDB leg of the same blocker. The epic seat narrowed this in the S1 thread, and the seat recorded it as claim amendment 6729595741 on #31682.

- On MariaDB 11, neither a partial unique nor a functional key part over `TEXT` columns can be built. The #31682 dev measured this live in Docker. S1 (PR #31727) therefore retires the old `(metadata_type, name)` index there only when the package-less guard exists physically. Without the guard, that old index keeps refusing a second package's row of the same name. A fresh MariaDB database has no guard either.
- To build: a MariaDB route that keeps a store-enforced one-row guarantee for package-less rows and admits a second package's row. It must not leak a visible column into reads and must not draw a destructive drift reading. Measure it on a MariaDB cell. If no such route exists, name the measured reason and say what an E child must do on MariaDB before it writes `(package, name)` rows.
- Expected file surface added: `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/**` (the dialect arm) and `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/activation-ledger-packageless-index.ts` (S1's migration), plus tests.
- The "must land before the first E child that writes a second package's ledger row" line now covers both Mongo and MariaDB.

State change: `pm:queue` removed in this stroke. On every dialect the package-less activation ledger's one-row guard is now store-enforced through the widening. Mongo retires the narrower driver-built unique create-before-drop. MariaDB carries the guard as an invisible virtual hash column with a unique key, so driver-sql makes one safe `replace_unique_index`. The E children of epic #31527 that waited on this precondition can build from this `main`.
